title: Tool consensus + client replay heuristics (SDK notes)
content:
Overview:

This is a working sketch for an approach to make complex tool-calling flows more robust and debuggable for clients using the Hosted API. The core idea: introduce a compact, Raft-inspired consensus/ordering primitive between server-side tool-call orchestrators and short-lived local proxies so that streaming outputs which depend on multiple tool calls become deterministic and resumable. Pair that with an SDK-level client replay heuristic that can reconstruct partial sessions and avoid duplicate side-effects.

Why this feels necessary (problem statement):
- We increasingly see multi-tool pipelines during streaming responses (search->tool->synthesize->external-http). When a client drops and reconnects, naive replay either repeats side effects (re-sends payments, creates duplicates) or loses progress.
- Current fallbacks (idempotency tokens, server-side best-effort dedupe) are brittle across embedded third-party tools that don't support idempotency.
- SDK ergonomics: developers want a simple reconnect experience: resume from where the UI left off, get a continuous transcript, and not have to deal with tool-side dedupe logic.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Deterministic ordering of tool calls that appear in the streamed transcript even when requests are routed across ephemeral workers.
- Minimal per-session metadata overhead (we're not adding multi-kilobyte logs per request).
- SDK-level resume API that (a) can transparently reattach to an in-progress session, (b) replays only safe operations or replays with a safe guardrail, and (c) surfaces a clear developer signal when manual dedupe is required.
- Observability hooks: per-tool-call traces, latency/cost breakdown, and an easy way to export a replayable session snapshot for debugging.

Non-goals:
- Not solving every third-party tool's idempotency semantics. We'll provide patterns and opinionated defaults, not force all integrations to be idempotent.
- Not a full distributed database/transaction system. This is a compact ordering + resume pattern optimized for inference flows, not general-purpose consistency.

Protocol sketch (server-side compact consensus):
- Session leader: each active session has a lightweight leader token (session-leader-id) owned by the chosen orchestrator for that user-session. Leader is a short-lived lease (30s) that can be transferred.
- Compact log: orchestrator emits a small per-session append-only log of tool-call intents with schema-lite frames: {frame_id, intent_type, tool_id, args_hash, idempotency_hint, side_effect_scope}. We'll keep frames < 512 bytes on average.
- Replica verification: other workers that may execute tool calls verify leader-signed frames before executing. If a worker receives a resume request it can fetch the compact log and replay deterministically.
- Consensus-lite: rather than full Raft, use leader-signed frames + monotonic sequence numbers + optional ack from a minimal set of standby orchestrators (2) for safety on leader failover. This keeps latency low but avoids dual-execution during leader transfer.

Client SDK resume/replay heuristics (ergonomics):
- Lightweight session token (session_id + resume_cursor). SDK exposes: resumeSession(session_token, onEvent) and provides events with frame-level markers.
- On reconnect: SDK fetches compact log up to resume_cursor and computes which frames were committed and which were only proposed. Heuristic table:
  - side_effect_scope: "safe-read" -> re-execute freely
  - "idempotent-or-hedged" -> safe to retry (server may attach idempotency-token)
  - "unsafe" -> SDK will not retry; instead it surfaces a "manual-confirm" event containing the pre-signed frame and a one-click developer callback to confirm replay.
- Subscription resilience: SDK maintains a small local buffer of in-flight frames and their argument hashes; if server signals that a frame committed, SDK moves cursor forward; otherwise it will attempt seamless reattach up to N=3 times before surfacing developer action.

Structured output + transcript stitching:
- Each frame produces typed output envelope: {frame_id, phase: partial|final, content_type, payload_hash, schema_version}. SDK stitches partial frames in-order and renders progressive fidelity.
- For complex multi-tool responses we establish stable insertion points in the transcript tied to frame ids so clients can apply local diffs deterministically. This reduces UI flicker on reconnection.

Failure modes and mitigation:
- leadership flip while tool-calls executing -> standby ack requirement (small window) or server-side compensation handlers that mark a frame as "compensated" and emit compensating frames.
- third-party tool side-effects executed twice -> mark as "unsafe" and require developer confirmation; also provide server-side compensation templates when integrations support reversal (e.g., DELETE or refund).
- long-lived sessions (>30 min) -> leader lease rotation strategy + checkpointing of compact logs to durable store (daily or per-N frames).

Telemetry & observability:
- expose per-frame metrics: time-to-sched, time-to-exec, total-cost, tool-latency. Tie traces to tokens so customer support can replay exact transcripts.
- add SDK debug endpoint: exportReplaySnapshot(session_id, resume_cursor) -> returns the compact log + collected outputs in a compressed format for offline repro. (This should be gated by RBAC.)

SDK ergonomics (developer experience):
- keep public API small: startSession(params)->Session, Session.on(event)->, Session.resume(token)->, Session.exportDebugSnapshot()->
- default SDK behavior: optimistic resume for safe frames, safe-guard manual flow for unsafe frames; logs visible as structured warnings that can be toggled off.
- built-in UI helpers (React hook examples) in SDK to rehydrate transcript and show a "Continue" button when manual replay is needed.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (alpha): behind feature flag for internal teams and a small set of customers. Basic leader lease + compact log read; no acking; SDK can resume read-only flows.
- Phase 1 (beta): add standby acks, simple idempotency hints, and manual-confirm SDK flow. Start instrumenting telemetry and support export snapshots.
- Phase 2 (GA): default on for hosted-api streaming sessions with tool-calling enabled; migration guides for integrations; document compensation patterns with sample adapters.

Open questions / TODOs:
- exact frame schema (minimal vs descriptive). Tradeoff: more metadata helps debugging but increases payload. Need perf benchmarks. TODO: bench frames at different sizes (JIRA-API-3421).
- leader failover semantics vs latency budget: what's the acceptable hedging window? proposal: 50ms local failover + compensate frames. Sync with SRE.
- UX for manual-confirm: should SDK keep a local dry-run or must it always surface server-signed frame? (security/attestation question)
- legal/compliance: design audit trail for billing and side-effectful calls. Add to security review.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is ideation — aim is to capture constraints we keep hitting in customer callbacks and reduce accidental duplicates while preserving low-latency streaming UX.
- If you care about a specific integration (payments, ticketing, cms-ingest), add notes in the linked JIRA item and tag Lina.

Quick links / references:

- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-sdk/pull/918 (sketch of resume API)
